_source: Transcribed from the Claude Design handoff bundle's VENUES constant in Curia.dc.html (fetched 2026-07-30) — real illustrative seed venues, not chains, matching Hard rule 1. `reason` strings are the actual brand-voice match-reason copy from the prototype; use as the register/quality bar for new copy, not verbatim filler. Added by curia-moments-journeys (M6): The Old Cellars is transcribed from the prototype's own VENUES constant (this file was previously a 15-of-18 subset that happened to omit it, even though the prototype's own moments picks reference it by name). Everyman Cinema/Rudy's/Porta are transcribed from the prototype's own JOURNEYS constant (the 'Date Night in Altrincham' stops, which carry name/kind/note there but were never given a standalone VENUES entry in the prototype) — lat/lon/spend/base/bands for those three are new, plausible fill-ins (Altrincham town centre) rather than transcribed, since the prototype never assigned them any.
_metroScopeNote: A Los Angeles metro (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City — 31 real, independently-verified venues) existed here from an earlier 2026-08 pass and was removed at explicit later request (2026-08) to keep the app scoped to Manchester/Cheshire only. See docs/data/districts.json's own _metroScopeNote for the same removal on the district side.
_manchesterCheshireResearchSource: Happy Seasons, The Bull's Head, HOME, Band on the Wall, Manchester Art Gallery, Royal Exchange Theatre, and The Wine Cellar were added 2026-08 from the first run of the daily Manchester/Cheshire research pipeline (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md), manually reviewed and promoted (the automated review agent was down at the time — see .claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md for what that step normally does) rather than left in docs/data/venue-suggestions.json. All seven verified real, currently-operating, single-site or same-village-group venues via independent web sources (official sites, CAMRA, Tripadvisor, council/charity registries) — none are chains (Hard rule 1); The Bull's Head shares ownership with two sister pubs, both in the same village of Mobberley, the same precedent as this file's own Ivy Spinningfields/Craig's. Filled real gaps: Chinatown and Mobberley had zero prior venues, Deansgate had zero Do-category venues, and Do was the thinnest category city-wide. Happy Seasons introduced a new venue type, 'CANTONESE ROAST' (no existing Eat tile/type fit a roast-meats specialist) — mapped to the Eat category in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts so mood filtering still finds it, though no onboarding tile targets it specifically yet.
_cheshireExpansionSource: Altrincham Market, Sugo Pasta Kitchen, The Old Dancer, The Stolen Lamb, The Elk of Hale, Church Inn, and Aldeli were added 2026-08 at explicit user request to expand Cheshire's coverage, which at 8 venues across 5 districts was noticeably thinner than Manchester's. Manually researched and verified one at a time via direct web search (not the automated pipeline) — real, currently-operating, single-site or small-regional-group venues, checked against Hard rule 1 the same way as the entries above; two strong candidates (Yara, Eastern Revive) were dropped despite being independent and family-run because their 5-6-site regional footprints read closer to a small chain than a same-village group, and a third (Victors, Alderley Edge) was dropped because it's a second branch of the Hale Victors already seeded here and would have collided on the same slugified id. Church Inn is Bull's Head's actual sister pub (same Cheshire Cat Pubs & Bars group, same village) — a real instance of the ownership pattern already flagged above, not a new one; a third sibling (Roebuck Inn, also Mobberley) was found but skipped to avoid three venues from one seven-pub group sitting in a single small village. Filled real gaps: Altrincham Market gives Cheshire its first Do-category venue with real liveliness (Everyman Cinema was previously the only one); Aldeli introduces a new type, 'BRUNCH SPOT', for the 'Brunch' onboarding tile, which previously matched zero venues anywhere in the app — mapped in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts. 'ALE HOUSE' (The Old Dancer, since removed — see _closureNote below) and 'GREEK TAVERNA' (The Stolen Lamb) are also new types, left Drink/Eat category-only for now (like CANTONESE ROAST) since no existing onboarding tile fits either precisely.
_wilmslowDensitySource: 20 venues added 2026-08 at explicit user request — a deliberate density test ('so we can test how the matchmaking works close to me with a semi densely populated town'), targeting 5 Drink / 7 Eat / 10 Do specifically for Wilmslow, plus Wilmslow Golf Club (added alongside, but seeded in Mobberley — see below). Landed at 4 Drink / 7 Eat / 10 Do (21 Wilmslow venues total including the two already there) after extensive individual research: Wilmslow's bar scene turned out to be unusually chain-heavy for a Cheshire town (excluded, with real footprints checked: Slug & Lettuce, The Botanist, Revolution, Unico Lounge [part of 'The Lounges', 200+ sites], Anthology [Greene King-owned, since renamed The Swan Inn], The King William [Robinsons Brewery], Stanneylands Hotel [now JW Lees-owned, the same chain already excluded once for Alderley Edge Hotel]) — a 5th genuine independent wasn't found after a good-faith search, so 4 is the honest number rather than a padded one. Every included venue passed the same single-site/small-local-group Hard rule 1 screen as prior passes; Cibo, Suburban Green, Smoke Wilmslow, Heddy's and Caramello are all real 2-site sibling pairs (their other sites: Didsbury, Chorlton, Chorlton, Alderley Edge, Didsbury respectively) — the same precedent already established for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields/Sugo. Wilmslow Golf Club is real and genuinely called that, but its actual grounds sit in Great Warford, within Mobberley's territory, not Wilmslow's — seeded there by real location rather than by name. Closed 5 real onboarding-tile coverage gaps that had zero matching venues anywhere in the app: 'Parks & green space' (The Carrs), 'Cookery & craft' (Wilmslow Kitchen), 'Walking tours' (Wilmslow History Tours), 'Late-night lounges' (Symposium), and 'Spectator sport' (Wilmslow RUFC and Wilmslow Golf Club) — plus extended 'Markets', which already had Mackie Mayor/Altrincham Market, to its first artisan-market example (Wilmslow Artisan Market). See src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts for the mappings. Introduced 14 new venue types; most are Eat/Drink category-only (no tile fits precisely, same treatment as CANTONESE ROAST) since a small town's real venues don't sort neatly into the tile catalog's higher-end city categories.
_closureNote: The Old Dancer (16 Grove Street, Wilmslow) was removed 2026-08, one day after being added in the pass above, on direct user report that it has permanently closed — independent web sources (Yelp, Tripadvisor) still listed it as open as of this same date, so this is trusted local/current knowledge outweighing lagging listing sites, not independently re-corroborated. No dangling Moment/Journey references existed to clean up. Its 'ALE HOUSE' type mapping in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts was left in place (harmless, ready for a future venue of that type) rather than removed, matching how other now-unused-but-still-mapped types are handled. This prompted two changes to the daily research/review agent briefs (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md, .claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md): checking a candidate is real and non-chain was never the same as checking it's still open today, and neither brief previously re-verified already-promoted venues at all — see those files' own updated 'still operating' guidance. Sugo Pasta Kitchen (Altrincham) removed 2026-09-04: renamed to Sud in early 2023 (a trademark dispute with an unrelated Glasgow restaurant also called Sugo), then Sud closed all four Greater Manchester sites permanently on 31 December 2023. A same-site business now trading as 'Rigatoni's' is a separate, unrelated venture, not a Sud/Sugo rebrand or continuation — confirmed by direct user correction 2026-09-04 after an earlier automated pass (on a since-superseded branch, never merged) conflated the two; not independently re-added here, since a genuinely different business needs its own Hard rule 1 verification from scratch, not inherited trust from the venue it happens to have replaced. 'HANDMADE PASTA' type mapping in tile-catalog-map.ts (Eat|Chef's counter) left in place, same precedent as ALE HOUSE above — Sugo was its only venue, but the type stays ready for a future one.
_prestburyCheadleHulmeKnutsfordVenueSour: First venues for the three districts added 2026-09-03 (see docs/data/districts.json's own note on why those districts exist) — manually researched one at a time via direct web search, not the automated pipeline, at explicit user request ('they need venues now'). Ownership verified for every candidate before inclusion, same Hard rule 1 bar as prior passes: Ye Olde Admiral Rodney and the Church Inn (Cheadle Hulme) were found and dropped — both Robinsons Brewery tied houses, the same regional brewery already excluded once for Wilmslow's King William; Village Pub & Grill (Cheadle Hulme) was dropped as part of the 34-site Village Hotels group; John Millington (Cheadle Hulme) was dropped as a Hydes Brewery tied house. Wallop (Knutsford) is a real 3-site group (Knutsford/Prestwich/Didsbury) — the same small-sibling-group precedent as Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. LI~LY introduces 'TASTING MENU' onto an existing type/tile; Bacchus introduces 'CHAMPAGNE BAR', mapped to the real 'Champagne bars' onboarding tile in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts, which previously matched zero venues anywhere in the app; Delhi Dream introduces 'INDIAN RESTAURANT', left category-only (Eat) like CANTONESE ROAST/GREEK TAVERNA since no existing tile fits precisely. Cheadle Hulme stays thin (one venue) rather than padded — a second good-faith search (Coffee Fix Cafe, Coco's Cafe) didn't turn up anything with strong enough verification to include yet, the same 'honest number, not a padded one' call already made for Wilmslow's Drink category.

_dietaryPetSource: 2026-09-04: added real per-venue `petFriendly`/`dietaryOptions` to every one of the 97 venues, fixing a hard-filter bug found via a matchmaking test against the live scoring engine — src/lib/data/seed.ts previously hardcoded `petFriendly: false` and `dietaryOptions: ['none']` for every venue, so any user with a real dietary requirement or travelling with a pet got zero results, always (CLAUDE.md's Matchmaking contract makes both hard filters, not soft weights, so a wrong `true` here is worse than a conservative `false`). Researched one venue at a time via direct web search (venue's own site, Tripadvisor, dedicated allergen/dog-friendly directories) — `petFriendly: true` only where a source explicitly confirmed general pet dogs are welcome (assistance-dog-only policies, a standard UK legal accessibility requirement at galleries/theatres/cinemas, do NOT count and are left `false`); `dietaryOptions` only includes an option where a source explicitly confirmed it (a dedicated vegetarian/vegan menu section, an allergen/gluten-free listing, etc.) — never inferred from venue type alone. Where a venue genuinely couldn't be confirmed either way after a real search (roughly a third of entries — mostly small independents with no detailed web presence, or non-food Do venues like galleries/studios), both fields were left at the safe conservative default (`false`/`['none']`) rather than guessed; this means some real venues that likely do accommodate a dietary need or pet still show as unconfirmed, which is the honest state of what's publicly verifiable, not a remaining bug. Two incidental closure signals surfaced during this pass and were NOT acted on here (out of scope for this task, flagged for the next closure-audit-style check): Riva Bar & Restaurant (Hale) — recent reviews suggest it closed a few weeks ago; The Yard (Alderley Edge) — one source ('the times they are a-changin') describes its cafe/shop as having closed at some point.

_wilmslowCoordinateCorrectionSource: 2026-09-08, at explicit user report: standing physically at Smoke Wilmslow, the app showed ~500m away instead of ~0. Confirmed real: Smoke's stored coordinate (53.3286,-2.2288) vs. its real postcode centroid (44 Water Lane, SK9 5AP -> 53.326556,-2.235888, via postcodes.io, the free UK Ordnance-Survey-backed postcode API) differ by almost exactly 520m. This exposed that this file's long-repeated 'street-level precision' claim wasn't actually true for most of Wilmslow's 22 venues — coordinates there were closer to rough estimates than real geocodes (Wilmslow Kitchen was off by ~2.9km, actually on Deanway Trading Estate north of town, not central Wilmslow; Wilmslow RUFC by ~1.9km). Fixed all 22 by finding each venue's real current postcode via direct web search (its own site, food-hygiene-rating registries, Companies House, etc. — not inherited from a prior pass) and geocoding via postcodes.io. Two pairs of venues genuinely do share one postcode (Wine Cellar/Suburban Green/Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness at SK9 1AA, Heddy's/Caramello at SK9 5BB) because they're real next-door/same-building neighbours on Hawthorn Lane and Water Lane respectively — not a research shortcut, confirmed from each one's own independently-found address. This is a Wilmslow-only pass; the same likely-imprecise-coordinate issue probably exists elsewhere in this file (every district added before this date used the same by-eye coordinate approach) and needs the same real-postcode-geocoding treatment, not assumed fixed just because Wilmslow now is.
_muckyPupSource: 2026-09-08, at explicit user request ('add smoke, woodfire smoke, juniper, and the mucky pup in wilmslow'): only The Mucky Pup (15 Grove Street, Wilmslow) was added. 'Smoke' was already in this file as 'Smoke Wilmslow' (44 Water Lane, added 2026-08) — a genuinely different, already-seeded business from Wood Fire Smoke (31 Water Lane), not a duplicate suggestion. Wood Fire Smoke and Juniper were both researched and, at the user's own decision after being shown the finding, deliberately NOT added: Wood Fire Smoke has 4 confirmed sites (Wilmslow, Macclesfield, Congleton, Sale) and its own coverage describes it as 'expanding beyond Cheshire'; Juniper has grown to 5 sites (Wilmslow, Hale, Bramhall, Stockton Heath, plus a newly opened Manchester city-centre site on St Ann's Street) — both real, independently-owned, genuinely good businesses, but both past the 2-3-site sibling-pair line this file has held everywhere else (see the 2026-08 Cheshire expansion note's rejection of Yara/Eastern Revive on the same basis). The Mucky Pup itself is confirmed single-site, real, currently trading (family-run Irish bar/live music venue, opened ~2024) — no chain footprint found anywhere. Coordinates are street-level (Grove Street, matching Wilmslow Artisan Market/Symposium's existing precision on the same street), not per-building GPS. Type mapped to the existing GASTROPUB type (food + drink + live music, same category as Wilmslow Tavern/Charlie Brown's Hale) rather than introducing a new type, since it fits reasonably well. dietaryOptions left at ['none'] on real evidence, not a gap: one source explicitly states the menu has no gluten-free options, and no vegetarian/vegan confirmation was found elsewhere; petFriendly left false — no dog-friendly confirmation found despite a direct search.

venues.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
venues.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.

venues.name: Erst
venues.reason: Natural wine and communal tables both on, and the kitchen runs to 11pm.

venues.name: Schofield's
venues.reason: Award-winning list, mixology at the table — the fullest version of your cocktail tile.

venues.name: Mana
venues.reason: Michelin-recognised with a chef's table; one step above your spend dial.

venues.name: 20 Stories
venues.reason: Skyline view and heated outdoor seating — the heaters matter tonight.

venues.name: The Jane Eyre
venues.reason: Booth seating and no music you have to shout over.

venues.name: Blinker
venues.reason: Unmarked entrance on Tib Street; speakeasy-style still weighted on.

venues.name: Matt & Phreds
venues.reason: Live sets to 1am, intimate seating, no cover before nine.

venues.name: The Ivy Spinningfields
venues.reason: Formal service and a dress code; late sittings to 10.30pm.

venues.name: Refuge
venues.reason: Live pianist Thursday to Saturday, service well past midnight.

venues.name: Tattu
venues.reason: Set menus and dessert theatrics; loudest room in the district after nine.

venues.name: Victors
venues.reason: Communal tables on, group-friendly buzz — worth the drive on a Friday.

venues.name: Pollen Bakery
venues.reason: Canalside counter seats and viennoiserie out of the oven at eight.

venues.name: Mackie Mayor
venues.reason: Nine kitchens under one roof — the easiest room in the city to arrive at without a plan.

venues.name: Foundation Coffee
venues.reason: A mill floor big enough to work in, and nobody rushing the second cup.

venues.name: The Wizard
venues.reason: Fires lit from October, and the Edge walk finishes at the door.

venues.name: The Old Cellars
venues.reason: Sommelier on site and small plates until close.

venues.name: Everyman Cinema
venues.reason: Sofa seats in screen two. Order the wine before the trailers — they bring it to you.

venues.name: Rudy's
venues.reason: No bookings, but the queue after the late screening is usually nothing.

venues.name: Porta
venues.reason: One last sherry standing at the counter. Kitchen closes at midnight.

venues.name: Happy Seasons
venues.reason: Forty-odd years on Faulkner Street, and the queue for the roast duck still forms before the doors do.

venues.name: The Bull's Head
venues.reason: Named best pub in Cheshire, then best in the whole North West, and Mill Lane still has more sheep on it than sat-nav.

venues.name: HOME
venues.reason: Five screens, two stages and a gallery floor that's changed again by the time you've finished your coffee downstairs.

venues.name: Band on the Wall
venues.reason: A stage bolted high on the far wall since the thirties, reborn after a £3.5m rebuild — the room where the touring act you half-recognise turns out to be the whole point of the night.

venues.name: Manchester Art Gallery
venues.reason: Free to walk in off Mosley Street and stand in front of the Pre-Raphaelites; the current dress-and-textile show, WORN, quietly reframes how you look at your own coat on the way out.

venues.name: Royal Exchange Theatre
venues.reason: A glass module dropped into a Victorian trading hall — the largest theatre-in-the-round in the world, close enough that the actors' footsteps land in your chest.

venues.name: The Wine Cellar
venues.reason: Forty wines by the glass and a slate of Courtyard Dairy cheese on a Hawthorn Lane side street — the sort of place you mean to leave after one and don't.

venues.name: Altrincham Market
venues.reason: Ten independent kitchens and two bars under one market roof, open till ten most nights — arrive hungry and undecided, leave neither.

venues.name: The Stolen Lamb
venues.reason: Chef-owned Greek on Water Lane, island-leaning rather than taverna-cliché — the lamb chops are why regulars stopped reading past them.

venues.name: Suburban Green
venues.reason: Sister site to the Chorlton original, four doors down Hawthorn Lane from its own sibling Wine Cellar — small plates built to share and a list that never repeats a wine twice a week.

venues.name: Smoke Wilmslow
venues.reason: Four generations of curing and smoking behind the bar snacks — Water Lane's café by day, cocktail room by night, same kitchen either way.

venues.name: Symposium
venues.reason: Grove Street's latest late licence — upstairs booths built for the hour after everywhere else has called last orders.

venues.name: Cibo
venues.reason: Family-run on Green Lane, a retractable roof over the terrace and a hundred and sixty covers that still feel like a neighbourhood table.

venues.name: Heddy's
venues.reason: Water Lane institution now with a second room in Alderley Edge — the mezze arrives before you've finished deciding what else to order.

venues.name: Caramello
venues.reason: Didsbury's original brunch room found a second home on Water Lane — scratch-made plates and a queue that starts before ten.

venues.name: Wilmslow Tavern
venues.reason: Simon and Kay's village-centre local out toward Dean Row — proper pizza, a beer garden, and nobody rushing you off the table.

venues.name: Phanthong Thai
venues.reason: Mum-and-daughter run on Alderley Road, next door to the King's Arms — the menu reads long and somehow everything on it is right.

venues.name: Vietbowl
venues.reason: Family-run home-style cooking on Bank Square — the kind of pho you'd get told to slow down and finish properly.

venues.name: Rex Cinema
venues.reason: Art deco since 1936, dark for two decades, reborn in 2019 — plush seats, a proper bar, and the original REX signage still over the door.

venues.name: The Carrs
venues.reason: Seventy-one acres along the Bollin, gifted to the town by a Boddington and named for the Norse word for bog-meadow — the walk that clears a working week.

venues.name: Wilmslow Kitchen
venues.reason: Sarah and David Bridge's school on the Deanway estate, tucked behind a row of Ferrari and Porsche showrooms — evening classes end with everyone sitting down to eat what they made.

venues.name: Ricardo Van Parmar Gallery
venues.reason: Private viewings by appointment on Alderley Road — the stock runs from emerging names to originals by Banksy and Warhol, and nobody hurries you round.

venues.name: Wilmslow Artisan Market
venues.reason: Grove Street and Bank Square close to traffic once a month for a hundred stalls of food, craft and live music — check the date before you plan an evening around it.

venues.name: Wilmslow RUFC
venues.reason: Memorial Ground on Kings Road, a co-operatively owned club pitched between the Carrs and the river — North West 1 rugby with a proper clubhouse pint after.

venues.name: Green Room Theatre
venues.reason: A Victorian cottage and an old shirt factory, converted by the town's own amateur society — founded in 1924, one of the oldest in the country, and still selling out a hundred-and-two-seat house.

venues.name: Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness
venues.reason: Above a bakery on Hawthorn Lane, the same studio Tracey has taught from for over twenty years — small classes, monthly sound ceremonies, no scale in sight.

venues.name: Wilmslow History Tours
venues.reason: Free, two hours, departs the library at eleven — the Historical Society's own guide walks you into St Bartholomew's, on a site with a church since 1246.

venues.name: Alchemy Personal Training
venues.reason: A private studio off Hawthorn Walk, wet room and changing rooms included — one-to-one sessions, not a class timetable to fit yourself around.

venues.name: Wilmslow Golf Club
venues.reason: Great Warford's eighteen holes since the 1880s, shaped in turn by James Braid and Frederick Hawtree — Open qualifying history on a course most of Cheshire only plays as a guest.

venues.name: The Elk of Hale
venues.reason: Family-run since 2013 on Ashley Road, an Alpine-lodge fit-out that shouldn't work in Cheshire and does — the spirits list runs deeper than the room.

venues.name: Church Inn
venues.reason: Opposite the twelfth-century church it's named for, and named best pub in the country more than once since — book the snug or don't bother.

venues.name: Aldeli
venues.reason: A former car showroom turned New York deli on London Road — salt beef bagels before noon, pancakes after.

venues.name: Hallé St Peter's
venues.reason: A deconsecrated Grade II church on Blossom Street, still the Hallé's own rehearsal hall — public concerts land in a room built for hymn acoustics, not a sound engineer.

venues.name: BAB NQ
venues.reason: Flatbreads made from scratch in an open theatre kitchen, and a basement cocktail room that only unlocks once the sun's properly down.

venues.name: Smolensky Gallery
venues.reason: Polished concrete and street-art pedigree inside the ABC Building on Quay Street — worth a detour on the way to dinner, not an afterthought once you've eaten.

venues.name: Podium Restaurant
venues.reason: Two AA Rosettes some forty floors below Cloud 23, and a kitchen more assured than the view it's sitting under.

venues.name: Hale Country Club & Spa
venues.reason: Five thermal rooms and an infinity pool looking out over its own acreage of Cheshire countryside — a members' club that still takes you for the day.

venues.name: Barnshaw Smithy
venues.reason: Poached eggs and proper coffee next to a working reclamation yard, on the lane between Mobberley and Ashley that the sat-nav still hesitates over.

venues.name: Nam
venues.reason: Manchester's only true audiophile sound system, assembled by the team behind London's Brilliant Corners, running in the basement of a Vietnamese kitchen that keeps going long after the DJs start.

venues.name: ATOMECA Wine Bar
venues.reason: Schofield's own second act on The Avenue — a walk-in wine list built around small plates, not the cocktail menu working next door.

venues.name: Hope Mill Theatre
venues.reason: A converted cotton mill on Pollard Street, opened by two directors chasing Off West End intimacy — Fringe Venue of the Year, and every seat close enough to see the actors breathe.

venues.name: Another Hand
venues.reason: Twenty-four covers up a flight of painted steps on Deansgate Mews, low-intervention plates built around whatever Cinderwood's growers sent over that morning.

venues.name: King Street Townhouse Spa
venues.reason: A subterranean ESPA spa under a Grade II Italianate former bank on King Street, Himalayan salt cave included — the infinity pool upstairs is for residents, the day spa isn't.

venues.name: Evelyn's Cafe Bar
venues.reason: Brunch classics by day, then the charcoal Inka grill takes over after dark — Persian and Pan-Asian small plates in a room that never quite decides which meal it's for, on purpose.

venues.name: Waugh Brow Farm Shop
venues.reason: Dave and Ruth Jones's own cattle and pigs, twenty yards from the counter that sells them — a working farm since 1985, with a café tacked on for people who came for bacon and stayed for cake.

venues.name: Flawd Wine
venues.reason: A waterside bottle shop on the New Islington marina that doubles as a bar — walk-ins only, a cheese board built to match whatever's open, and a wine list that skips anything you'd call conventional.

venues.name: Reserve at The Rex
venues.reason: Three separate terraces above a former bank on King Street, each with its own name and its own hour of the day it does best — arrive before the swing band starts if you want a seat outside.

venues.name: Riddles
venues.reason: A 1920s room the size of a living room on Greenwood Street, yards from the market — Emma's own list of Prohibition-era cocktails, poured by people who mean it.

venues.name: Speak In Code
venues.reason: No sign on Jackson's Row, just a door — inside, entirely plant-based small plates and a cocktail list built on the bar's own fermentations, running to 2am.

venues.name: Bar Shrimp
venues.reason: Seafood snacks and cocktails under one mood-lit roof on New York Street, built by the Higher Ground and Flawd team around a sound system that does as much of the work as the bar.

venues.name: Manchester Rare Books
venues.reason: A former waiting room on platform one, stocked with pre-loved and hard-to-find titles, plus a shelf of film and music ephemera nobody's rushing you to buy.

venues.name: Charlie Brown's Hale
venues.reason: The former GupShup site on Ashley Road, made over into a corner gastro bar — signature cocktails alongside the food, for once, rather than an afterthought.

venues.name: esea contemporary
venues.reason: The UK's only art centre built around East and Southeast Asian practice, in an RIBA award-winning Market Buildings conversion on Thomas Street — free to walk into, and worth the detour even mid-crawl.

venues.name: Mobberley Cricket Club
venues.reason: Founded 1876, still on Church Lane — a clubhouse bar and a viewing rail looking out over a Cheshire outfield, the same unhurried afternoon it's always been.

venues.name: Bacchus
venues.reason: A dedicated Champagne bar and a wine list built by the owners themselves, in a converted Village cottage — Mike Williams' kitchen behind it once ran Moss Nook.

venues.name: The Legh Arms
venues.reason: Twelve ensuite rooms above a 17th-century coaching inn on the Village green — the kind of place that turns a dinner booking into a reason to stay over.

venues.name: Delhi Dream
venues.reason: Mahipal and Sunita's own kitchen on Turves Road — proper Punjabi cooking that never bothered opening a second site.

venues.name: LI~LY
venues.reason: Aiden Byrne's tasting menu inside a 400-year-old timbered building on King Street — three AA Rosettes and a Michelin Guide listing for a room that seats a genuine handful.

venues.name: Wallop
venues.reason: A neighbourhood wine bar with two small siblings in Didsbury and Prestwich, live music some nights and a King Street terrace that fills first.

venues.name: Archive Bar & Bottle
venues.reason: Two floors on Mellor Road — real ale downstairs, a proper gin and cocktail list up top, and nobody rushing you between them.

venues.name: Thorn Grove Park
venues.reason: Seven and a half acres in the middle of the village — bowls green, open lawn, and nowhere near as busy as the postcode suggests.

venues.name: The Olde School
venues.reason: A converted schoolroom on the Village green, open four days a week for wholesome plates and coffee, with a wine list nobody expects from a place this size.

venues.name: Oil Art Advisory Gallery
venues.reason: Zoe Garner's own two floors on King Street, opened 2024 — emerging names alongside the established, and nobody hurrying your second lap.

venues.name: Little Yang Sing
venues.reason: A basement on the George Street corner, twenty-odd years into the same Cantonese repertoire — the dim sum trolley Chinatown's newer rooms still measure themselves against.

venues.name: Hale Wine Bar
venues.reason: Folding windows onto Ashley Road and a list built by someone who left the big pub groups to pour it properly.

venues.name: La Cucina
venues.reason: Wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta on London Road, cocktails at the same counter — the kind of independent Alderley Edge's chain-heavy strip could use more of.

venues.name: Dexter & Jones
venues.reason: A thousand beers and three hundred gins behind the counter, but it's Adam and Katy Rickitt's own wine picks worth pulling up a stool for.

venues.name: Contemporary Six Hale
venues.reason: Alex Reuben's second room, on Ashley Road in the space Clark Art left behind — contemporary names given the same quiet run of wall as the Manchester original.

venues.name: Wong Wong Bakery
venues.reason: Twenty-plus years on Princess Street, family-run, and the egg tarts are usually gone by mid-afternoon on a Saturday.

venues.name: Rococo
venues.reason: Taz and her daughter Faye's own shop on the high street — soft furnishings, glassware and one dressing-up rail of preloved designer pieces at the back.

venues.name: The Foxhole
venues.reason: Kip Evans' own boutique bar — gins from round the world, four craft beers on tap, and a cheeseboard built to match whichever bottle you land on.

venues.name: Lilac Cottage Tapas & Wine Bar
venues.reason: Haseena and Felipe's own oak-beamed cottage on New Road — tapas built for sharing, and a wine list that doesn't rush you to decide.

venues.name: Chads Theatre
venues.reason: A hundred-and-four-seat house run by the town's own amateur society since just after the First World War — four main plays and two youth productions a year, coffee lounge included.

venues.name: Bruntwood Park
venues.reason: Vibrant gardens and a duck pond a short walk from the station — the kind of park that turns a Sunday into an actual plan.

venues.name: Inventery
venues.reason: Ian Jones' own free-of-tie bar in a former retail unit on Station Road — cocktails and small plates, nothing about it tied to a brewery's price list.

venues.name: Manchester Craft and Design Centre
venues.reason: Eighteen working studio boutiques inside a converted Victorian fish and poultry market on Oak Street — watch a maker at the bench, then buy the piece straight from the hands that shaped it.

venues.name: The Horsfall
venues.reason: A three-storey Victorian shop on Great Ancoats Street, named for the philanthropist who opened the country's first art museum here in 1884 — free exhibitions and open studio sessions, run by the mental health charity that revived the building.

venues.name: Bar Etna
venues.reason: Sicilian, family-run, and unbothered by the market's queues two streets over — fresh pasta and pistachio everything from a kitchen that still mans its own deli counter.

venues.name: Knutcraft at the Ruskin Rooms
venues.reason: A Grade II-listed former reading room and fire station on Drury Lane, now a pottery-painting studio running Bring Your Own Bottle evenings for adults who'd rather glaze a plate than scroll past one.

venues.name: Mobberley Ice Cream Coffee House
venues.reason: A working dairy farm on Church Lane doing its own ice cream, its own coffee roast and a proper afternoon tea — order the sundae, then walk it off past the herd that made it.

venues.name: Yuzu
venues.reason: Twenty-five covers on Faulkner Street, no bookings for most sittings, BYOB, and a ramen broth that's been simmering since before Chinatown's newer rooms opened — a queue since 2012 that still hasn't thinned.

venues.name: One Eight Six
venues.reason: A barbershop by day on the old Deansgate courthouse corner; find the mirrored door after dark and it's live soul and Motown running until the small hours.

venues.name: Arcane
venues.reason: A basement two friends built off King Street, no sign worth mentioning above ground — cocktails poured without the queue Deansgate's louder rooms carry.

venues.name: KLUB
venues.reason: A one-woman-built rooftop salon above Manchester Hall's old Freemasons' hall — one-to-one treatments, not a treatment-room timetable to fit yourself around.

venues.name: Portland Wine
venues.reason: An Ashley Road institution that still runs its own tastings — a glass of fizz on arrival, five wines poured properly, and a port to finish before you've decided what to take home.

venues.name: Contemporary Six
venues.reason: Alex Reuben's original room on Princess Street, by the Town Hall's side door — forty-odd artists on rotation, an Own Art scheme that lets you pay monthly, and the space that later gave Hale its own quieter twin.

venues.name: K2 Karaoke
venues.reason: Thirty private booths across two George Street floors, right in the middle of the streets that are Chinatown before Chinatown is anything else — the one real answer here to a night that wants its own soundtrack.

venues.name: Pip
venues.reason: Mary-Ellen McTague's return to the city she left Aumbry in, cooking low-waste, seasonal British plates on the ground floor of the Treehouse — a Michelin Guide listing within its first year.

venues.name: Portfolio
venues.reason: Julian Pizer and Cameron Foster's own cellar made public on Bridge Street — 250-odd Champagnes from more than seventy growers, a wall of a hundred bottles to read while you decide, and a menu of single-bite dishes built to match whichever one you land on.

venues.name: HARCOURT
venues.reason: Brian Hung and Priscilla So's Hong Kong-inspired free house on Stamford New Road — fourteen taps of proper cask and craft, and small plates built from Hong Kong's own street-food repertoire rather than a brewery's set menu.

venues.name: Butchers Bar
venues.reason: Turtons' old shop on Ashley Road, empty three years, reborn as Ben Shepherd's own stage and skylight — cocktails poured at the counter where the meat used to hang, and live sets most nights rather than a jukebox.

venues.name: Neki
venues.reason: Daniel Nechita's own room on King Street since 2019 — scratch-made brunch, paninis and a house coffee blend nobody else in Knutsford is pouring.

venues.name: Mobberley Village Bakers
venues.reason: Thirty-four years trading under the Goostrey's name on Town Lane, and still the reason half the village has flour on its hands before nine.

venues.name: Ancoats Coffee Co
venues.reason: Roasting on site inside Royal Mills since 2013 — the beans leave for cafés across the city every morning, but the counter seats here still get the first pour.

venues.name: The Edge Theatre & Arts Centre
venues.reason: A former Red Cross hospital on Manchester Road doing double duty as Chorlton's own theatre, gallery and community cinema — the programme changes hands often enough that a second visit rarely repeats the first.

venues.name: The Chorlton Tap
venues.reason: Wilbraham Road's real-ale room since the late nineties, back when it was just called The Bar — fourteen keg lines, four cask, and a wood-fired oven doing pizza out front on the nights it fancies it.

venues.name: Bar San Juan
venues.reason: Fifteen years on Beech Road and counting — proper Spanish tapas, sherry by the glass, and a Neighbourhood Venue of the Year plaque behind the bar the locals would tell you is deserved.

venues.name: White Peak Alpaca Farm
venues.reason: Jake and Joanna's own herd on Paddock Hill, pre-booked walks only — the sort of unhurried Cheshire afternoon that doesn't need a restaurant attached to justify the drive out.

venues.name: Inch Arts
venues.reason: The old town library's ground floor, now a working charity of studios, a makerspace and a gallery that changes hands as often as the artists teaching in it — free to walk into, on Stamford New Road.

venues.name: The Blind Pig
venues.reason: A courtyard door off King Street with no sign worth mentioning, four keg lines and a cocktail list that never quite repeats itself — Porto next door if the wait's too long.

venues.name: InHale Yoga
venues.reason: A first-floor studio on Cecil Road running vinyasa before work and ashtanga after it — small classes, real teachers' names on the timetable, not a franchise's booking app.

venues.name: Lions Den
venues.reason: Two hundred capacity on Deansgate Mews, built and still run by one promoter twenty years into the job — open mic on a Wednesday, a proper touring act by the weekend.

venues.name: Australasia
venues.reason: A glass pyramid entrance on The Avenue and a Pacific Rim share-plates menu re-set under new ownership last year — sushi and southeast Asian flavours in the basement room that started Spinningfields' whole restaurant scene back in 2011.

venues.name: Lime Tree
venues.reason: Chef-patron Patrick Hannity's own room on Lapwing Lane since 1987 — the menu turns over weekly, but the crispy duck stays by popular demand, and nobody's ever accused it of being stuffy.

venues.name: Volta
venues.reason: The Unabombers' Burton Road room — globally-inspired small plates and a Sunday roast worth planning round, dog-friendly and rarely in a hurry to turn the table.

venues.name: Saison
venues.reason: David Bell's beer-first successor to the old Violet Hour on Burton Road — a serious keg and cask list, small plates built to match it, cocktails for whoever didn't come for the beer.

venues.name: Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden
venues.reason: Ninety acres gifted to the city in 1915, rockery and alpine beds still doing their job long after the council funding that once made it official — ten minutes from the village and a different pace entirely.

venues.name: The Jane Eyre Chorlton
venues.reason: Ancoats' cocktail room did well enough to earn a second, bigger kitchen on Beech Road — the same curated list, more room for families at Sunday roast, and mahogany that doesn't feel bolted on for the occasion.

venues.name: Casa de Moor
venues.reason: Mediterranean small plates and a cocktail list in the old Zitano room on Beech Road — under the same ownership as Heaton Moor's Casa De Casa, though each kitchen now runs its own name and its own menu.

venues.name: Henry's Cafe
venues.reason: Natalie's own café in the old Post Office on The Village — homemade cakes, a dog under every second table, and nobody minding if breakfast runs into afternoon tea.

venues.name: Knutsford Heritage Centre
venues.reason: A reconstructed 17th-century forge on King Street, run entirely by volunteers — the Millennium Tapestry runs thirteen metres round two galleries, and admission is whatever you feel like leaving in the box.

venues.name: Altrincham Little Theatre
venues.reason: A hundred and thirty seats and a drama society older than the building it's in — amateur only in the sense that nobody's paid, not in the sense that anyone's amateur.

venues.name: Festival Hall
venues.reason: The parish's own 1927 assembly rooms, licensed bar included — comedy nights and orchestral programmes sharing a stage built for a music festival that's still running, just under a different name now.

venues.name: The Mucky Pup
venues.reason: An Irish bar on Grove Street with live sets Friday through Sunday, and a pint of Guinness regulars swear tastes like it was poured in Dublin.

venues.name: Where the Light Gets In
venues.reason: A Victorian coffee warehouse loft on Rostron Brow, Sam Buckley's tasting menu the reason Stockport now carries a Michelin Green Star of its own — locally sourced, seasonal, and cooked in full view of the room.

venues.name: Bruk
venues.reason: A small self-funded room on Little Underbank, poured by people who left the big groups to do it properly — the list turns over by the bottle, not the season.

venues.name: Stockport Market Hall
venues.reason: A Victorian glass-roofed hall on Market Place trading since the 1860s, thirty-odd independent stalls under one roof — turn up for a Foodie Friday and you won't leave with the plan you arrived with.

venues.name: FOLK
venues.reason: Four friends' own room on Burton Road, brunch plates giving way to small plates by evening — the covered terrace fills first, same as it's always done.

venues.name: Marie Louise Gardens
venues.reason: Four and three-quarter acres off Palatine Road, gifted to the city in 1903 and kept up since by the people who live around it — paved paths and flowering trees, a Green Flag on the gate and no rush to leave.

venues.name: Chorlton Bookshop
venues.reason: Family-run on Wilbraham Road since 1983, a local-authors shelf that actually means something and staff who'll find the thing you half-remember the plot of.

venues.name: Chorlton Water Park
venues.reason: A hundred and seventy acres of lake, woodland and meadow ten minutes past the tram stop — the walk Chorlton takes when Beech Road's got too loud.

venues.name: Giovanni's
venues.reason: The old Post Office at the Tatton Park end of King Street, no group behind it — proper homemade Italian and a Sunday lunch that still runs to a queue.

venues.name: Corks Out
venues.reason: A wine specialist and off-licence on London Road with one sister room out in Stockton Heath — tastings most weeks, and a list built by people who'd rather talk you out of the safe bottle.

venues.name: The Seven Oaks
venues.reason: A white faience freehouse on the Art Gallery corner of Chinatown, still pulling proper cask after the louder rooms have called last orders — real ale, real cider, and pie and mash that doesn't apologise for being unfashionable.

venues.name: Savoy Cinema
venues.reason: Art deco since the 1920s, dark for years, reborn in 2015 under the same family who run two more just like it in Belper and Melton Mowbray — 180 velvet seats, a licensed bar, and a programme that still mixes new releases with classics rather than picking one.

venues.name: Heaton Social
venues.reason: Shaw Road's old oriental restaurant made over into a wine-and-cocktails room under local ownership since January 2025 — a neat beer garden out back, a function room downstairs, and a landlord whose roots in Heaton Moor go back further than the venue does.

venues.name: Cure Bistro
venues.reason: Mehmed and David's own room on Heaton Moor Road since May last year — a rotating French and Mediterranean menu with the cocktail list treated as seriously as the kitchen, not bolted on as an afterthought.

venues.name: Bar Caput
venues.reason: The same two chefs who earned Cantaloupe its Michelin Bib Gourmand have reopened the same Great Underbank room as a Roman aperitivo bar — fritti, osteria plates and a cocktail called the Bicycle Thief, built to be a Tuesday habit rather than a once-a-year booking.

venues.name: Trattoria D'Agostino
venues.reason: Marco D'Agostino's own kitchen on Station Road since 2010, family-run and single-site by choice — a quarter-century of Italian cooking behind a menu that never bothered opening a second dining room to prove it.

venues.name: Sip Wine Bar
venues.reason: Nick Yates' Enomatic wall on Burton Road, pouring by the glass so you can try before committing to the bottle — cheese and charcuterie built to match, and regulars who've learned by now to book.

venues.name: Prestbury Golf Club
venues.reason: A Harry Colt course laid out on Macclesfield Road in 1920, good enough to sit inside England's top hundred — a proper members' round a mile past the Village's antique shops and timbered pubs.

venues.name: The Beer House
venues.reason: Manchester Road's cask specialist since 2000, sold out of the Marble Brewery stable in 2018 and free of any tie since — five years running as Trafford & Hulme CAMRA's own Pub of the Year, and a patio that fills before the taps do.

venues.name: The Garden Eatery
venues.reason: Kate and Amy's plant-led room on Ashley Road since 2014 — daytime only, dairy and meat optional rather than absent, and a queue for the sweetcorn fritters that starts most mornings before ten.

venues.name: The Edge
venues.reason: The wooded sandstone ridge the whole village takes its name from, National Trust-managed since 1948 — Engine Vein and the Druids' Circle a fifteen-minute walk apart, real caves nobody's quite meant to still be exploring, and the actual reason The Wizard's regulars turn up muddy.

moments.title: Best for Date Night
moments.blurb: Low light, tables for two, and a wine list worth staying for a third glass.

moments.title: Entertaining a Client
moments.blurb: Quiet enough to talk. Expensive enough to register without being said out loud.

moments.title: Big Group of Friends
moments.blurb: Rooms that can take eight at short notice without a sigh from the host.

moments.title: Solo Reset
moments.blurb: Counter seats, a book, and nobody asking whether you're waiting for someone.

journeys.title: Date Night in Altrincham
journeys.blurb: A film first so there's something to talk about, then eight minutes on foot to the best pizza in the county.

journeys.title: A Client, Well Handled
journeys.blurb: Height first for the view, then somewhere with tablecloths and a sommelier who knows when to leave you alone.
